+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Pushes a folder of screenshots to the orphan `ci-shots` branch so they can be read without an artifact token.
+# Usage: ci/publish-shots.sh SRC_DIR LANE   (LANE: ios | admin-desktop | admin-phone ...)
+# Lands in ci-shots:<pr-N|branch>/<LANE>/, replacing the previous run's files for that lane.
+set -euo pipefail
+src=$(cd "$1" && pwd); lane=$2
+scope=${PR_NUMBER:+pr-$PR_NUMBER}; scope=${scope:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME//\//-}}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+
+git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+if git fetch --depth=1 origin ci-shots 2>/dev/null; then
+  git worktree add --detach "$work" FETCH_HEAD
+else
+  git worktree add --detach "$work"
+  git -C "$work" checkout --orphan ci-shots-new
+  git -C "$work" rm -rfq --ignore-unmatch .
+fi
+
+dest="$work/$scope/$lane"
+rm -rf "$dest" && mkdir -p "$dest"
+cp -R "$src"/. "$dest"/
+printf '{"sha":"%s","run":"%s/%s/actions/runs/%s","at":"%s"}\n' "${HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}" "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL" "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "$dest/meta.json"
+
+cd "$work"
+git add -A
+git commit -qm "$scope/$lane @ ${HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}" || exit 0
+for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
+  git push -q origin HEAD:ci-shots && exit 0
+  sleep $((attempt * 3))
+  git pull -q --rebase origin ci-shots
+done
+exit 1

+# 08 · Mac + Xcode setup (and how Claude sees the iOS app)
+
+One-time setup for the MacBook, about 45 minutes. You do this part. After it, Claude can build and check the iPhone app two ways.
+
+## How the bridge works
+
+```
+                 ┌──────────── Lane 1: cloud (always on) ────────────┐
+ Claude (cloud) ─┤ push code → GitHub Mac runner:                     │
+      ▲          │   start local API → seed demo data (Playwright)    │
+      │          │   → iPhone simulator → tap every screen (XCUITest) │
+      │          │   → screenshots → ci-shots branch + PR checks      │
+      └──────────┤ ← Claude reads logs + screenshots, fixes, pushes   │
+                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+
+                 ┌──────────── Lane 2: your Mac (when it is open) ────┐
+ Claude Code  ───┤ XcodeBuildMCP → Xcode + simulator on your Mac      │
+ (on the Mac)    │ build, run, tap, screenshot, read logs, live       │
+                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+- **Lane 1** is the main one. Each pull request runs `.github/workflows/ios.yml` (app) and `.github/workflows/worker.yml` (API + admin console in a real browser). Screenshots land on the `ci-shots` branch under `pr-<number>/ios`, `pr-<number>/admin-desktop` and `pr-<number>/admin-phone`.
+- **Lane 2** is for fast, hands-on work. A Claude Code session running *on your Mac* drives the simulator directly.
+- Neither lane needs a paid Apple Developer account. You only need one to put the app on a real iPhone or TestFlight (Phase 7).
+
+## 1 · Xcode
+
+1. Mac App Store → install **Xcode** (26 or newer). Open it once and accept the license. When asked which platforms to install, pick **iOS**.
+2. Terminal:
+   ```bash
+   sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app
+   xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
+   xcrun simctl list devices available | grep iPhone   # should list iPhones
+   ```
+3. Optional, for help inside Xcode: **Xcode → Settings → Intelligence** → sign in with your Claude account.
+
+## 2 · Tools
+
+```bash
+/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"   # Homebrew, if missing
+brew install xcodegen node@22 git
+```
+
+## 3 · Get the code
+
+```bash
+mkdir -p ~/Downloads/"AI projects" && cd ~/Downloads/"AI projects"
+git clone https://github.com/djbatalona06/Empire.git
+cd Empire
+```
+
+## 4 · Run the API (terminal tab 1)
+
+```bash
+cd worker && npm ci && cd ..
+e2e/start-api.sh          # migrates, loads demo data, serves http://localhost:8787
+```
+
+Leave it running. Open http://localhost:8787 and sign in as `admin@dealerdoor.test` to see the admin console.
+
+## 5 · Your first Xcode build (terminal tab 2)
+
+```bash
+cd e2e && npm ci && npm run seed:customer && cd ..   # adds customer@dealerdoor.test with an order + invoices
+cd ios && xcodegen && open DealerDoor.xcodeproj
+```
+
+In Xcode, pick an iPhone simulator at the top, then press **⌘R**. Sign in as:
+
+| Who | Email |
+|---|---|
+| Field coworker | `rep1@dealerdoor.test` |
+| Customer | `customer@dealerdoor.test` |
+
+There's no password and no email to check. In development the app signs you in right away.
+
+To run the same UI tests CI runs: **⌘U** in Xcode, or
+```bash
+xcodebuild test -project DealerDoor.xcodeproj -scheme DealerDoor -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'
+```
+(swap in a simulator name from step 1 if `iPhone 16` isn't installed).
+
+`project.yml` is the source of truth. Run `xcodegen` again after pulling changes that add files. Don't edit `DealerDoor.xcodeproj` by hand; it's regenerated and ignored by git.
+
+## 6 · Lane 2: Claude Code on the Mac
+
+```bash
+npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
+cd ~/Downloads/"AI projects"/Empire
+claude mcp add XcodeBuildMCP -- npx -y xcodebuildmcp@latest mcp
+claude
+```
+
+Then ask: *"Build DealerDoor for the iPhone simulator, run it, sign in as rep1@dealerdoor.test and screenshot the route map."*
+
+- XcodeBuildMCP (open source, by Sentry) gives Claude tools to build, launch, tap, type and take screenshots in the simulator.
+- Optional: newer Xcode versions also ship their own MCP bridge (`xcrun mcpbridge`). Try `claude mcp add xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`. If the command isn't found, your Xcode doesn't have it yet, and XcodeBuildMCP covers everything.
+- Optional: turn on **Remote Control** in that session to steer it from your phone.
+
+## 7 · Watching progress
+
+- **PR checks**: `iOS app / ui-tests` and `Worker API / e2e` show ✅ or ❌. The run's **Summary** tab has a pass/fail table.
+- **Screenshots**: on GitHub, switch the branch picker to `ci-shots`. Claude also publishes a private "DealerDoor Build Progress" page after each round.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+| Symptom | Fix |
+|---|---|
+| App says "Couldn't load" | The API in tab 1 isn't running. Run `e2e/start-api.sh` again. |
+| Sign-in error in the simulator | Check http://localhost:8787 opens in Safari on the Mac. |
+| `xcodegen: command not found` | `brew install xcodegen` |
+| Customer tab is empty | `cd e2e && npm run seed:customer` |
+| Build error about signing | You picked a real iPhone. Pick a simulator until you have an Apple Developer account. |

+import { expect, test, type APIRequestContext } from '@playwright/test';
+
+// Walks the API in the same order the iOS app does, so a backend change that would break the app fails here first.
+// It also leaves a demo customer (customer@dealerdoor.test) with an order and invoices for the iOS customer UI test.
+
+const CUSTOMER = 'customer@dealerdoor.test';
+const DOOR = { lat: 47.437, lng: -122.277 }; // seeded property p1
+
+async function signIn(request: APIRequestContext, email: string) {
+  const sent = await request.post('/v1/auth/login', { data: { email } });
+  expect(sent.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const { dev_token } = await sent.json();
+  expect(dev_token, 'dev_token only exists in development').toBeTruthy();
+  const verified = await request.post('/v1/auth/verify', { data: { token: dev_token } });
+  expect(verified.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const { access_token } = await verified.json();
+  return { authorization: `Bearer ${access_token}` };
+}
+
+test('coworker → customer flow the iOS app depends on', async ({ request }) => {
+  const rep = await signIn(request, 'rep1@dealerdoor.test');
+  expect((await (await request.get('/v1/me', { headers: rep })).json()).role).toBe('coworker');
+
+  // Route tab
+  const routes = await (await request.get('/v1/routes/mine', { headers: rep })).json();
+  expect(routes[0].stops.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+  expect((await request.get('/v1/service-area', { headers: rep })).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  expect((await request.get('/v1/dnk/map', { headers: rep })).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const consent = await (await request.get('/v1/consent-texts', { headers: rep })).json();
+  expect(JSON.stringify(consent)).toContain('v1');
+
+  // Lead capture at the door
+  const leadId = crypto.randomUUID();
+  const lead = await request.post('/v1/leads', {
+    headers: rep,
+    data: {
+      id: leadId, property_id: 'p1', customer_name: 'Casey Customer', phone: '206-555-0100', email: CUSTOMER,
+      product_interest: ['internet'], tcpa_accepted: true, disclosure_accepted: true, consent_text_version: 'v1', ...DOOR,
+    },
+  });
+  expect(lead.status()).toBe(201);
+  const svc = await (await request.post(`/v1/leads/${leadId}/serviceability`, { headers: rep, data: {} })).json();
+  expect(svc.serviceable).toBe(true);
+
+  const order = await request.post('/v1/orders', { headers: rep, data: { lead_id: leadId, skus: ['AIR', 'TV-STREAM'] } });
+  expect(order.status()).toBe(201);
+  const orderId = (await order.json()).id as string;
+
+  // Office schedules the install and bills two dealer fees: one paid, one still open.
+  const office = await signIn(request, 'office@dealerdoor.test');
+  const stages = await (await request.get(`/v1/orders/${orderId}/timeline`, { headers: office })).json();
+  const scheduled = stages.find((s: { stage: string }) => s.stage === 'install_scheduled');

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Copy UI-test screenshots out of an .xcresult and write a pass/fail summary.
+
+Usage: export-screenshots.py TestResults.xcresult OUT_DIR
+Writes OUT_DIR/<name>.png, OUT_DIR/results.json and prints a Markdown table (for $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY).
+"""
+import json, pathlib, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
+
+bundle, out = sys.argv[1], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+def xcresult(*args):
+    return subprocess.run(["xcrun", "xcresulttool", *args, "--path", bundle], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+
+# Screenshots: exported with UUID file names; the manifest maps them back to the names the tests gave them.
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+    xcresult("export", "attachments", "--output-path", tmp)
+    manifest = json.loads(pathlib.Path(tmp, "manifest.json").read_text())
+    for test in manifest:
+        for a in test.get("attachments", []):
+            name = re.sub(r"_\d+_[0-9A-F-]{36}", "", a["suggestedHumanReadableName"], flags=re.I)
+            shutil.copy(pathlib.Path(tmp, a["exportedFileName"]), out / name)
+
+# Per-test results
+results = []
+def walk(node):
+    if node.get("nodeType") == "Test Case":
+        failure = next((c["name"] for c in node.get("children", []) if c.get("nodeType") == "Failure Message"), "")
+        results.append({"test": node["name"], "result": node.get("result", "Unknown"), "failure": failure})
+    for child in node.get("children", []):
+        walk(child)
+for root in json.loads(xcresult("get", "test-results", "tests")).get("testNodes", []):
+    walk(root)
+(out / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
+
+print("| Test | Result | Why it failed |\n|---|---|---|")
+for r in results:
+    icon = "✅" if r["result"] == "Passed" else "❌"
+    print(f"| {r['test']} | {icon} {r['result']} | {r['failure'].replace('|', '/')} |")
+print(f"\n{len(list(out.glob('*.png')))} screenshots")

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Pushes a folder of screenshots to the orphan `ci-shots` branch so they can be read without an artifact token.
+# Usage: ci/publish-shots.sh SRC_DIR LANE   (LANE: ios | admin-desktop | admin-phone ...)
+# Lands in ci-shots:<pr-N|branch>/<LANE>/, replacing the previous run's files for that lane.
+set -euo pipefail
+src=$(cd "$1" && pwd); lane=$2
+scope=${PR_NUMBER:+pr-$PR_NUMBER}; scope=${scope:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME//\//-}}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+
+git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+if git fetch --depth=1 origin ci-shots 2>/dev/null; then
+  git worktree add --detach "$work" FETCH_HEAD
+else
+  git worktree add --detach "$work"
+  git -C "$work" checkout --orphan ci-shots-new
+  git -C "$work" rm -rfq --ignore-unmatch .
+fi
+
+dest="$work/$scope/$lane"
+rm -rf "$dest" && mkdir -p "$dest"
+cp -R "$src"/. "$dest"/
+printf '{"sha":"%s","run":"%s/%s/actions/runs/%s","at":"%s"}\n' "${HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}" "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL" "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "$dest/meta.json"
+
+cd "$work"
+git add -A
+git commit -qm "$scope/$lane @ ${HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}" || exit 0
+for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
+  git push -q origin HEAD:ci-shots && exit 0
+  sleep $((attempt * 3))
+  git pull -q --rebase origin ci-shots
+done
+exit 1

+# 08 · Mac + Xcode setup (and how Claude sees the iOS app)
+
+One-time setup for the MacBook, about 45 minutes. You do this part. After it, Claude can build and check the iPhone app two ways.
+
+## How the bridge works
+
+```
+                 ┌──────────── Lane 1: cloud (always on) ────────────┐
+ Claude (cloud) ─┤ push code → GitHub Mac runner:                     │
+      ▲          │   start local API → seed demo data (Playwright)    │
+      │          │   → iPhone simulator → tap every screen (XCUITest) │
+      │          │   → screenshots → ci-shots branch + PR checks      │
+      └──────────┤ ← Claude reads logs + screenshots, fixes, pushes   │
+                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+
+                 ┌──────────── Lane 2: your Mac (when it is open) ────┐
+ Claude Code  ───┤ XcodeBuildMCP → Xcode + simulator on your Mac      │
+ (on the Mac)    │ build, run, tap, screenshot, read logs, live       │
+                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+- **Lane 1** is the main one. Each pull request runs `.github/workflows/ios.yml` (app) and `.github/workflows/worker.yml` (API + admin console in a real browser). Screenshots land on the `ci-shots` branch under `pr-<number>/ios`, `pr-<number>/admin-desktop` and `pr-<number>/admin-phone`.
+- **Lane 2** is for fast, hands-on work. A Claude Code session running *on your Mac* drives the simulator directly.
+- Neither lane needs a paid Apple Developer account. You only need one to put the app on a real iPhone or TestFlight (Phase 7).
+
+## 1 · Xcode
+
+1. Mac App Store → install **Xcode** (26 or newer). Open it once and accept the license. When asked which platforms to install, pick **iOS**.
+2. Terminal:
+   ```bash
+   sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app
+   xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
+   xcrun simctl list devices available | grep iPhone   # should list iPhones
+   ```
+3. Optional, for help inside Xcode: **Xcode → Settings → Intelligence** → sign in with your Claude account.
+
+## 2 · Tools
+
+```bash
+/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"   # Homebrew, if missing
+brew install xcodegen node@22 git
+```
+
+## 3 · Get the code
+
+```bash
+mkdir -p ~/Downloads/"AI projects" && cd ~/Downloads/"AI projects"
+git clone https://github.com/djbatalona06/Empire.git
+cd Empire
+```
+
+## 4 · Run the API (terminal tab 1)
+
+```bash
+cd worker && npm ci && cd ..
+e2e/start-api.sh          # migrates, loads demo data, serves http://localhost:8787
+```
+
+Leave it running. Open http://localhost:8787 and sign in as `admin@dealerdoor.test` to see the admin console.
+
+## 5 · Your first Xcode build (terminal tab 2)
+
+```bash
+cd e2e && npm ci && npm run seed:customer && cd ..   # adds customer@dealerdoor.test with an order + invoices
+cd ios && xcodegen && open DealerDoor.xcodeproj
+```
+
+In Xcode, pick an iPhone simulator at the top, then press **⌘R**. Sign in as:
+
+| Who | Email |
+|---|---|
+| Field coworker | `rep1@dealerdoor.test` |
+| Customer | `customer@dealerdoor.test` |
+
+There's no password and no email to check. In development the app signs you in right away.
+
+To run the same UI tests CI runs: **⌘U** in Xcode, or
+```bash
+xcodebuild test -project DealerDoor.xcodeproj -scheme DealerDoor -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'
+```
+(swap in a simulator name from step 1 if `iPhone 16` isn't installed).
+
+`project.yml` is the source of truth. Run `xcodegen` again after pulling changes that add files. Don't edit `DealerDoor.xcodeproj` by hand; it's regenerated and ignored by git.
+
+## 6 · Lane 2: Claude Code on the Mac
+
+```bash
+npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
+cd ~/Downloads/"AI projects"/Empire
+claude mcp add XcodeBuildMCP -- npx -y xcodebuildmcp@latest mcp
+claude
+```
+
+Then ask: *"Build DealerDoor for the iPhone simulator, run it, sign in as rep1@dealerdoor.test and screenshot the route map."*
+
+- XcodeBuildMCP (open source, by Sentry) gives Claude tools to build, launch, tap, type and take screenshots in the simulator.
+- Optional: newer Xcode versions also ship their own MCP bridge (`xcrun mcpbridge`). Try `claude mcp add xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`. If the command isn't found, your Xcode doesn't have it yet, and XcodeBuildMCP covers everything.
+- Optional: turn on **Remote Control** in that session to steer it from your phone.
+
+## 7 · Watching progress
+
+- **PR checks**: `iOS app / ui-tests` and `Worker API / e2e` show ✅ or ❌. The run's **Summary** tab has a pass/fail table.
+- **Screenshots**: on GitHub, switch the branch picker to `ci-shots`. Claude also publishes a private "DealerDoor Build Progress" page after each round.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+| Symptom | Fix |
+|---|---|
+| App says "Couldn't load" | The API in tab 1 isn't running. Run `e2e/start-api.sh` again. |
+| Sign-in error in the simulator | Check http://localhost:8787 opens in Safari on the Mac. |
+| `xcodegen: command not found` | `brew install xcodegen` |
+| Customer tab is empty | `cd e2e && npm run seed:customer` |
+| Build error about signing | You picked a real iPhone. Pick a simulator until you have an Apple Developer account. |

+import { expect, test, type APIRequestContext } from '@playwright/test';
+
+// Walks the API in the same order the iOS app does, so a backend change that would break the app fails here first.
+// It also leaves a demo customer (customer@dealerdoor.test) with an order and invoices for the iOS customer UI test.
+
+const CUSTOMER = 'customer@dealerdoor.test';
+const DOOR = { lat: 47.437, lng: -122.277 }; // seeded property p1
+
+async function signIn(request: APIRequestContext, email: string) {
+  const sent = await request.post('/v1/auth/login', { data: { email } });
+  expect(sent.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const { dev_token } = await sent.json();
+  expect(dev_token, 'dev_token only exists in development').toBeTruthy();
+  const verified = await request.post('/v1/auth/verify', { data: { token: dev_token } });
+  expect(verified.ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const { access_token } = await verified.json();
+  return { authorization: `Bearer ${access_token}` };
+}
+
+test('coworker → customer flow the iOS app depends on', async ({ request }) => {
+  const rep = await signIn(request, 'rep1@dealerdoor.test');
+  expect((await (await request.get('/v1/me', { headers: rep })).json()).role).toBe('coworker');
+
+  // Route tab
+  const routes = await (await request.get('/v1/routes/mine', { headers: rep })).json();
+  expect(routes[0].stops.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+  expect((await request.get('/v1/service-area', { headers: rep })).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  expect((await request.get('/v1/dnk/map', { headers: rep })).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const consent = await (await request.get('/v1/consent-texts', { headers: rep })).json();
+  expect(JSON.stringify(consent)).toContain('v1');
+
+  // Lead capture at the door
+  const leadId = crypto.randomUUID();
+  const lead = await request.post('/v1/leads', {
+    headers: rep,
+    data: {
+      id: leadId, property_id: 'p1', customer_name: 'Casey Customer', phone: '206-555-0100', email: CUSTOMER,
+      product_interest: ['internet'], tcpa_accepted: true, disclosure_accepted: true, consent_text_version: 'v1', ...DOOR,
+    },
+  });
+  expect(lead.status()).toBe(201);
+  const svc = await (await request.post(`/v1/leads/${leadId}/serviceability`, { headers: rep, data: {} })).json();
+  expect(svc.serviceable).toBe(true);
+
+  const order = await request.post('/v1/orders', { headers: rep, data: { lead_id: leadId, skus: ['AIR', 'TV-STREAM'] } });
+  expect(order.status()).toBe(201);
+  const orderId = (await order.json()).id as string;
+
+  // Office schedules the install and bills two dealer fees: one paid, one still open.
+  const office = await signIn(request, 'office@dealerdoor.test');
+  const stages = await (await request.get(`/v1/orders/${orderId}/timeline`, { headers: office })).json();
+  const scheduled = stages.find((s: { stage: string }) => s.stage === 'install_scheduled');
+  const at = new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 86_400_000).toISOString();
+  expect((await request.patch(`/v1/timeline/${scheduled.id}`, { headers: office, data: { status: 'complete', at } })).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+  const setup = await (await request.post('/v1/invoices', { headers: office, data: { order_id: orderId, amount_cents: 4900, payment_term_days: 0, description: 'Setup fee', send: true } })).json();
+  const wiring = await (await request.post('/v1/invoices', { headers: office, data: { order_id: orderId, amount_cents: 9900, payment_term_days: 30, description: 'Inside wiring', send: true } })).json();
+
+  // Customer app: My order, Invoices, pay (Stripe mock mode locally)
+  const customer = await signIn(request, CUSTOMER);
+  const mine = await (await request.get('/v1/orders', { headers: customer })).json();
+  expect(mine.some((o: { id: string }) => o.id === orderId)).toBe(true);
+  const detail = await (await request.get(`/v1/orders/${orderId}`, { headers: customer })).json();
+  expect(detail.timeline.map((s: { key: string }) => s.key)).toContain('install_scheduled');
+  expect(JSON.stringify(detail)).not.toContain('note_internal');
+
+  const paid = await (await request.post(`/v1/invoices/${setup.id}/pay`, { headers: customer, data: { method: 'card' } })).json();
+  expect(paid.invoice.status).toBe('paid');
+  const open = await (await request.get(`/v1/invoices/${wiring.id}`, { headers: customer })).json();
+  expect(open.status).toBe('viewed');
+  expect((await request.get('/v1/feedback/customer/mine', { headers: customer })).ok()).toBeTruthy();
+});

+import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';
+
+// Every sidebar section of the admin console, at desktop and phone width. Screenshots feed the progress gallery.
+const SECTIONS = ['overview', 'review', 'routes', 'dnk', 'leads', 'orders', 'invoices', 'feedback', 'scorecards', 'commissions', 'catalog', 'users', 'settings', 'audit'];

+  const errors: string[] = [];
+  page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push(e.message));
+  page.on('console', (m) => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push(m.text()); });
+
+  await page.goto('/');
+  await page.locator('#login-form input[name=email]').fill('admin@dealerdoor.test');

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Copy UI-test screenshots out of an .xcresult and write a pass/fail summary.
+
+Usage: export-screenshots.py TestResults.xcresult OUT_DIR
+Writes OUT_DIR/<name>.png, OUT_DIR/results.json and prints a Markdown table (for $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY).
+"""
+import json, pathlib, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
+
+bundle, out = sys.argv[1], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+def xcresult(*args):
+    return subprocess.run(["xcrun", "xcresulttool", *args, "--path", bundle], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+
+# Screenshots: exported with UUID file names; the manifest maps them back to the names the tests gave them.
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+    xcresult("export", "attachments", "--output-path", tmp)
+    manifest = json.loads(pathlib.Path(tmp, "manifest.json").read_text())
+    for test in manifest:
+        for a in test.get("attachments", []):
+            name = re.sub(r"_\d+_[0-9A-F-]{36}", "", a["suggestedHumanReadableName"], flags=re.I)
+            shutil.copy(pathlib.Path(tmp, a["exportedFileName"]), out / name)
+
+# Per-test results
+results = []
+def walk(node):
+    if node.get("nodeType") == "Test Case":
+        failure = next((c["name"] for c in node.get("children", []) if c.get("nodeType") == "Failure Message"), "")
+        results.append({"test": node["name"], "result": node.get("result", "Unknown"), "failure": failure})
+    for child in node.get("children", []):
+        walk(child)
+for root in json.loads(xcresult("get", "test-results", "tests")).get("testNodes", []):
+    walk(root)
+(out / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
+
+print("| Test | Result | Why it failed |\n|---|---|---|")
+for r in results:
+    icon = "✅" if r["result"] == "Passed" else "❌"
+    print(f"| {r['test']} | {icon} {r['result']} | {r['failure'].replace('|', '/')} |")
+print(f"\n{len(list(out.glob('*.png')))} screenshots")

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Pushes a folder of screenshots to the orphan `ci-shots` branch so they can be read without an artifact token.
+# Usage: ci/publish-shots.sh SRC_DIR LANE   (LANE: ios | admin-desktop | admin-phone ...)
+# Lands in ci-shots:<pr-N|branch>/<LANE>/, replacing the previous run's files for that lane.
+set -euo pipefail
+src=$(cd "$1" && pwd); lane=$2
+scope=${PR_NUMBER:+pr-$PR_NUMBER}; scope=${scope:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME//\//-}}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+
+git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+if git fetch --depth=1 origin ci-shots 2>/dev/null; then
+  git worktree add --detach "$work" FETCH_HEAD
+else
+  git worktree add --detach "$work"
+  git -C "$work" checkout --orphan ci-shots-new
+  git -C "$work" rm -rfq --ignore-unmatch .
+fi
+
+dest="$work/$scope/$lane"
+rm -rf "$dest" && mkdir -p "$dest"
+cp -R "$src"/. "$dest"/
+printf '{"sha":"%s","run":"%s/%s/actions/runs/%s","at":"%s"}\n' "${HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}" "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL" "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "$dest/meta.json"
+
+cd "$work"
+git add -A
+git commit -qm "$scope/$lane @ ${HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}" || exit 0
+for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
+  git push -q origin HEAD:ci-shots && exit 0
+  sleep $((attempt * 3))
+  git pull -q --rebase origin ci-shots
+done
+exit 1

+# 08 · Mac + Xcode setup (and how Claude sees the iOS app)
+
+One-time setup for the MacBook, about 45 minutes. You do this part. After it, Claude can build and check the iPhone app two ways.
+
+## How the bridge works
+
+```
+                 ┌──────────── Lane 1: cloud (always on) ────────────┐
+ Claude (cloud) ─┤ push code → GitHub Mac runner:                     │
+      ▲          │   start local API → seed demo data (Playwright)    │
+      │          │   → iPhone simulator → tap every screen (XCUITest) │
+      │          │   → screenshots → ci-shots branch + PR checks      │
+      └──────────┤ ← Claude reads logs + screenshots, fixes, pushes   │
+                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+
+                 ┌──────────── Lane 2: your Mac (when it is open) ────┐
+ Claude Code  ───┤ XcodeBuildMCP → Xcode + simulator on your Mac      │
+ (on the Mac)    │ build, run, tap, screenshot, read logs, live       │
+                 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+- **Lane 1** is the main one. Each pull request runs `.github/workflows/ios.yml` (app) and `.github/workflows/worker.yml` (API + admin console in a real browser). Screenshots land on the `ci-shots` branch under `pr-<number>/ios`, `pr-<number>/admin-desktop` and `pr-<number>/admin-phone`.
+- **Lane 2** is for fast, hands-on work. A Claude Code session running *on your Mac* drives the simulator directly.
+- Neither lane needs a paid Apple Developer account. You only need one to put the app on a real iPhone or TestFlight (Phase 7).
+
+## 1 · Xcode
+
+1. Mac App Store → install **Xcode** (26 or newer). Open it once and accept the license. When asked which platforms to install, pick **iOS**.
+2. Terminal:
+   ```bash
+   sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app
+   xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
+   xcrun simctl list devices available | grep iPhone   # should list iPhones
+   ```
+3. Optional, for help inside Xcode: **Xcode → Settings → Intelligence** → sign in with your Claude account.
+
+## 2 · Tools
+
+```bash
+/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"   # Homebrew, if missing
+brew install xcodegen node@22 git
+```
+
+## 3 · Get the code
+
+```bash
+mkdir -p ~/Downloads/"AI projects" && cd ~/Downloads/"AI projects"
+git clone https://github.com/djbatalona06/Empire.git
+cd Empire
+```
+
+## 4 · Run the API (terminal tab 1)
+
+```bash
+cd worker && npm ci && cd ..
+e2e/start-api.sh          # migrates, loads demo data, serves http://localhost:8787
+```
+
+Leave it running. Open http://localhost:8787 and sign in as `admin@dealerdoor.test` to see the admin console.
+
+## 5 · Your first Xcode build (terminal tab 2)
+
+```bash
+cd e2e && npm ci && npm run seed:customer && cd ..   # adds customer@dealerdoor.test with an order + invoices
+cd ios && xcodegen && open DealerDoor.xcodeproj
+```
+
+In Xcode, pick an iPhone simulator at the top, then press **⌘R**. Sign in as:
+
+| Who | Email |
+|---|---|
+| Field coworker | `rep1@dealerdoor.test` |
+| Customer | `customer@dealerdoor.test` |
+
+There's no password and no email to check. In development the app signs you in right away.
+
+To run the same UI tests CI runs: **⌘U** in Xcode, or
+```bash
+xcodebuild test -project DealerDoor.xcodeproj -scheme DealerDoor -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'
+```
+(swap in a simulator name from step 1 if `iPhone 16` isn't installed).
+
+`project.yml` is the source of truth. Run `xcodegen` again after pulling changes that add files. Don't edit `DealerDoor.xcodeproj` by hand; it's regenerated and ignored by git.
+
+## 6 · Lane 2: Claude Code on the Mac
+
+```bash
+npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
+cd ~/Downloads/"AI projects"/Empire
+claude mcp add XcodeBuildMCP -- npx -y xcodebuildmcp@latest mcp
+claude
+```
+
+Then ask: *"Build DealerDoor for the iPhone simulator, run it, sign in as rep1@dealerdoor.test and screenshot the route map."*
+
+- XcodeBuildMCP (open source, by Sentry) gives Claude tools to build, launch, tap, type and take screenshots in the simulator.
+- Optional: newer Xcode versions also ship their own MCP bridge (`xcrun mcpbridge`). Try `claude mcp add xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`. If the command isn't found, your Xcode doesn't have it yet, and XcodeBuildMCP covers everything.
+- Optional: turn on **Remote Control** in that session to steer it from your phone.
+
+## 7 · Watching progress
+
+- **PR checks**: `iOS app / ui-tests` and `Worker API / e2e` show ✅ or ❌. The run's **Summary** tab has a pass/fail table.
+- **Screenshots**: on GitHub, switch the branch picker to `ci-shots`. Claude also publishes a private "DealerDoor Build Progress" page after each round.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+| Symptom | Fix |
+|---|---|
+| App says "Couldn't load" | The API in tab 1 isn't running. Run `e2e/start-api.sh` again. |
+| Sign-in error in the simulator | Check http://localhost:8787 opens in Safari on the Mac. |
+| `xcodegen: command not found` | `brew install xcodegen` |
+| Customer tab is empty | `cd e2e && npm run seed:customer` |
+| Build error about signing | You picked a real iPhone. Pick a simulator until you have an Apple Developer account. |

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Copy UI-test screenshots out of an .xcresult and write a pass/fail summary.
+
+Usage: export-screenshots.py TestResults.xcresult OUT_DIR
+Writes OUT_DIR/<name>.png, OUT_DIR/results.json and prints a Markdown table (for $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY).
+"""
+import json, pathlib, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
+
+bundle, out = sys.argv[1], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+def xcresult(*args):
+    return subprocess.run(["xcrun", "xcresulttool", *args, "--path", bundle], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+
+# Screenshots: exported with UUID file names; the manifest maps them back to the names the tests gave them.
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+    xcresult("export", "attachments", "--output-path", tmp)
+    manifest = json.loads(pathlib.Path(tmp, "manifest.json").read_text())
+    for test in manifest:
+        for a in test.get("attachments", []):
+            name = re.sub(r"_\d+_[0-9A-F-]{36}", "", a["suggestedHumanReadableName"], flags=re.I)
+            shutil.copy(pathlib.Path(tmp, a["exportedFileName"]), out / name)
+
+# Per-test results
+results = []
+def walk(node):
+    if node.get("nodeType") == "Test Case":
+        failure = next((c["name"] for c in node.get("children", []) if c.get("nodeType") == "Failure Message"), "")
+        results.append({"test": node["name"], "result": node.get("result", "Unknown"), "failure": failure})
+    for child in node.get("children", []):
+        walk(child)
+for root in json.loads(xcresult("get", "test-results", "tests")).get("testNodes", []):
+    walk(root)
+(out / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
+
+print("| Test | Result | Why it failed |\n|---|---|---|")
+for r in results:
+    icon = "✅" if r["result"] == "Passed" else "❌"
+    print(f"| {r['test']} | {icon} {r['result']} | {r['failure'].replace('|', '/')} |")
+print(f"\n{len(list(out.glob('*.png')))} screenshots")
